note:
Malcolm likes the skin-art band style and wants six variations combining it with the model holding a product, with the eye gaze varied across the set.

CLASS A, WHICH CHANGES EVERYTHING. Every earlier skin brief was class B — no product, so nothing to invent. The moment a bottle enters frame the reference-lock protocol applies: these ship with the approved packshots attached, and FLUX.2 is barred outright because it substitutes fictional brands that look clean and survive a fast review. Label lines are quoted verbatim per the label-text-must-be-quoted rule, and everything below the two headline lines is thrown OUT OF THE DEPTH OF FIELD rather than asked to be small — the fix proven on the carton stacks tonight, after 'too small to read' produced near-legible garbling instead.

PRODUCT: the Copper Peptide Advanced Repair Serum, the flagship. One product across all six so the set reads as a series rather than a catalogue. Say the word and any slot can carry a cream jar instead.

A TENSION WORTH NAMING. Seedream has the best label fidelity of any supplier and refuses bare-skin subjects every time; Luma and the Gemini pair pass the skin and are weaker on lettering. So the supplier that would render the bottle best is the one least likely to accept the brief. These are written as beauty-campaign shots with a product rather than as nudes — head and shoulders, the product held — which should widen the field. If Seedream still refuses across the set, that is the answer to a question worth having asked.

EYE GAZE varies deliberately: closed, to camera, away and up, lowered to the product, back over the shoulder, closed with the head tipped. Malcolm's standing note on this project is that varied gaze is what stopped the review models looking like one shoot.

TYPE ZONE unchanged: the headline is centred, so a horizontal band through the middle of the frame stays even in tone, and the bottle and the eyes sit clear of it.

slots.title: Profile, eyes closed, bottle held at the jaw
slots.prompt: Extreme close-up fine-art beauty photograph of one woman around thirty five years old lying with her head tipped back, seen in profile from the side and slightly above, her eyes closed and her expression calm. Skin fills the frame edge to edge: décolleté across the lower left, the long sweep of the throat rising to the right, the jaw, cheekbone and closed lips at the upper right. One hand with five slender relaxed fingers holds the serum bottle upright against the side of her jaw, the bottle in sharp focus and label turned to camera. The bottle is a 30ml frosted DEEP BLUE glass dropper bottle with square shoulders, a brushed satin neutral silver-grey collar and a white rubber-bulb pipette, exactly as in the reference images. Legible type on it reads only: the Skingenetix DNA-helix mark with the wordmark 'Skingenetix', then 'COPPER PEPTIDE', then 'ADVANCED' and 'REPAIR SERUM'. Every remaining line falls outside the depth of field, visibly soft and blurred beyond any possibility of being read. Print no word that is not quoted here. Background beyond her a deep graphite grey, colour #1A1A1A, dark and even. One hard key light from the upper right rims the jaw and the shoulder of the bottle. Skin real and finely textured, visible pores, fine down, unretouched. A horizontal band through the middle of the frame stays even in tone with nothing crossing it.
